const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: summary_redacted.md
+L001 The user requested a lightweight local evaluation setup that copied only required dependencies and reused existing evaluation assets, avoiding execution from a large source tree.
+L002 The user required credentials and endpoints to come from environment-provided configuration without exposing their values and asked whether the evaluation assets and code were being reused from an earlier framework.
+L003 For CPU-only batch work, the user preferred designated partitions and asked for that preference to become reusable guidance; temporary fallback partitions were later authorized for the session without changing the standing preference.
+L004 The user repeatedly requested job progress and health checks, emphasizing that expected output files mattered more than a completed scheduler state alone.
+L005 The requested candidate set expanded to several paid and free models, and the user required separate credential pools for the two groups while allowing concurrent execution.
+L006 The user requested explicit job dependencies for some candidates and considered parallelizing a particularly slow candidate only if doing so would preserve service health.
+L007 The user requested a reusable analysis script measuring simulated-user tokens per turn with a shared tokenizer, average simulated-user turns for multi-turn tasks, and human-ground-truth statistics when available.
+L008 The report needed aggregate model comparisons across a profile-conditioned dataset and an interaction-style dataset and had to remain extensible for future model analyses.
+L009 The user asked which model acted as the assistant during role-playing, whether that behavior originated in the reused code, how changing it could affect scores, and whether the dataset recorded the assistant used during human-data collection.
+L010 The user then separated the judge, role-playing assistant, and final-document generator into fixed experimental roles and initially assigned the same compact model to all three for consistency.
+L011 The user requested reruns under the fixed-role setting while preserving completed result files, leaving one active job untouched, canceling an unlaunched dependent job, and scheduling the slowest candidate last.
+L012 The user asked the agent to verify that the fixed model was actually used in both judge and assistant roles.
+L013 The user later added two evaluator lanes for the profile-conditioned dataset and required them to judge existing trajectories rather than regenerate role-playing outputs or duplicate already-covered pairings.
+L014 The user designed an anonymous comparative evaluation in which randomly ordered responses from three candidates were jointly graded by multiple judges, with ties divided fractionally when calculating win rates.
+L015 The user observed that one candidate won less often than its peers despite receiving comparable absolute scores and requested a nuanced explanation rather than assuming that the evaluation was flawed.
+L016 The user requested subset-level win rates and scores and explicitly allowed analysis to proceed despite missing or incomplete results.
+L017 The user added a comparative style-similarity evaluation for the interaction-style dataset using the same candidate and judge groups, a fixed assistant, and previously generated trajectories.
+L018 For presentation, the user requested slide-ready independent and comparative plots, judge-specific ranks, and subset-level results, then clarified that two models should be excluded only as simulator candidates and retained as evaluators.
+L019 The user restricted the interaction-dataset reward to normalized writing-style and interaction-style similarity, combined by their mean, and excluded unrelated quality dimensions.
+L020 In the comparative setting, anonymous three-way grading used fractional tie handling rather than counting every tie as a full win or loss.
+L021 The user next requested plots for a naive-alignment measure from an existing audit run.
+L022 The agent separated the intended candidate lanes from supplemental lanes and excluded supplemental evaluator-as-candidate records from the requested plots.
+L023 Alignment records covered five represented subsets of the profile-conditioned dataset, while one additional subset was explicitly excluded; the interaction-style dataset had no alignment component.
+L024 The agent added a reusable alignment-data loader, regenerated the analysis snapshot, and produced aggregate and subset-level plots.
+L025 The interaction-style dataset instead contained source-identification and specificity evidence, so the agent treated naive profile alignment as unavailable there rather than fabricating a value.
+L026 The audit protocol defined `D_specificity` as a normalized real-versus-simulated specificity difference, `D_H` and `D_C` as source-score distances under two conditioning settings, and `D_audit = 0.5 D_specificity + 0.25 D_H + 0.25 D_C`; lower values were better.
+L027 To provide the requested source-distance term, the agent defined `D_source = (D_H + D_C) / 2`, making the composite equivalently `D_audit = 0.5 D_specificity + 0.5 D_source`.
+L028 The agent derived the distances only from the main audit lanes, excluded supplemental candidate runs, averaged evaluators equally, and weighted represented subsets equally within each dataset aggregate.
+L029 The component-level ordering did not always match the composite ordering, showing that an aggregate audit score could conceal which behavioral component drove a candidate's result.
+L030 The agent first produced a combined figure containing all three distances across aggregate and subset categories, with bars for equal-evaluator means and distinct markers for individual evaluators.
+L031 At the user's request, the agent split the result into three slide-ready figures, one for each distance, while initially retaining both aggregate and subset categories.
+L032 The user then simplified the presentation by removing subset categories and retaining only the two dataset aggregates in each standalone figure.
+L033 The final standalone figures used grouped candidate bars, evaluator-specific markers, and a common scale; the earlier combined figure remained available as a diagnostic overview.
+L034 An initial plot-generation attempt failed because it referenced a nonexistent local runtime path; correcting the path to the available workspace runtime allowed generation to succeed.
+L035 A primary raster renderer silently produced an incorrect image for one valid vector figure; the agent verified the vector source with an independent renderer and replaced the faulty raster output.
+L036 The agent visually inspected the generated figures and ran a syntax check on the reusable plotting program after the changes.
*** Add File: insight_redacted.md
+# I001
+Evidence: L009, L010, L013, L017, L018
+
+Evaluation roles should be modeled as separate experimental factors: candidate simulator, role-playing assistant, judge, and generator. Changing or filtering one role does not imply changing the others, so an explicit role matrix helps prevent accidental exclusions or unintended regeneration.
+
+# I002
+Evidence: L011, L013, L017, L022
+
+When trajectories are expensive to generate, new judges and comparative protocols can often reuse immutable trajectory outputs. Preserving earlier results and separating supplemental judge lanes from candidate-generation lanes enables new analyses without contaminating the original evaluation population.
+
+# I003
+Evidence: L014, L015, L020
+
+Absolute scores and comparative win rates answer different questions. A candidate can score close to its peers yet win infrequently when it is consistently slightly worse, and fractional tie handling further changes win-rate behavior; both measures are needed for a representative comparison.
+
+# I004
+Evidence: L023, L025, L026, L027
+
+Metrics should transfer across datasets only when their required inputs exist. When one dataset lacks the inputs for profile alignment but provides source and specificity evidence, a compatible aggregate can be defined from the available components without inventing a missing score.
+
+# I005
+Evidence: L022, L028
+
+Main evaluation lanes and supplemental candidate lanes require explicit provenance boundaries. Filtering by intended candidate membership prevents models introduced for supplemental judgments from silently entering the plotted candidate population.
+
+# I006
+Evidence: L023, L028
+
+Aggregation policy is part of the experimental result rather than a cosmetic plotting choice. Explicitly weighting evaluators and represented subsets makes aggregate means interpretable and avoids implying coverage for missing subsets or components.
+
+# I007
+Evidence: L026, L027, L029
+
+A composite audit distance can conceal component-level tradeoffs. Reporting source and specificity distances alongside the weighted composite makes it possible to identify which behavioral dimension drives an overall ordering.
+
+# I008
+Evidence: L030, L031, L032, L033
+
+Analytical completeness and presentation clarity benefit from separate artifacts. A detailed combined figure can support diagnosis, while one-metric aggregate figures are easier to communicate on slides; retaining both preserves evidence when presentation requirements become simpler.
+
+# I009
+Evidence: L004, L034, L035, L036
+
+Successful execution should be validated at the output level. Scheduler completion or a successful process exit is insufficient when runtime paths can be wrong or renderers can silently corrupt a figure; visual inspection and an independent rendering path can reveal failures missed by status checks.
+
+# I010
+Evidence: L023, L025, L028
+
+Coverage statements should enumerate represented subsets and available metric components instead of relying on a dataset-family label. Explicit coverage metadata prevents aggregate plots from implying observations that were never collected.
*** End Patch";
const result = await tools.apply_patch(patch);
text(result);
